title: BankWeaver: attackers gained admin access to a bank's Temenos Quantum Fabric without credentials
date_note: Article published November 20; it says investigators uncovered the breach in early September and gives no date for the intrusion itself.
org: Unnamed financial institution (Temenos Quantum Fabric customer)
summary: CyberPress reports a campaign it calls BankWeaver in which attackers got administrative access to a financial institution's Temenos Quantum Fabric deployment without valid credentials, because an internet-facing authentication service was configured for anonymous rather than private access. Two malicious Java components, FabricShell and FabricShadow, were used. Temenos released configuration updates and guidance; six other banks appeared to have the same configuration, with no breaches confirmed there.
plain: A report says attackers got into a bank's digital banking back end without a password because a login service was left open to anonymous access. The vendor has issued configuration guidance.
exec: A misconfigured, internet-exposed banking platform service reportedly gave attackers admin access; other banks may share the same setup.
action: Apply Temenos's configuration updates and guidance, set privileged authentication services to private, and remove direct internet access to Fabric and Spotlight administration services.
impact: Six other banks appeared to have the same configuration and internet exposure; no breaches were confirmed at them.

validation.note: Only CyberPress read; it credits Forescout but the Forescout and Temenos originals were not found in this run.

review.note: Title, summary, FabricShell and FabricShadow, anonymous auth cause, Temenos updates, six other banks without confirmed breaches checked against CyberPress 20 Nov; single_source correct
